sentences.text: Shri Kuldeep Singh - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri B.K. Upadhyay - Government Advocate for the respon Heard on I.A. No.25886/2025 , second application under Section 430 of BNSS, 2023/389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 09.02.2023.

Appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 363/34 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 03 years and fine of Rs.500/-, Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 05 years and fine of Rs.500, Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years and fine of Rs.500/- and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.500/-
respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
The appellant is charged for commission of rape with the victim.
The other co-accused have been enlarged on bail.
Appellant has no previous criminal history.
The appellant has already undergone about 07 years 09 months and 02 days.
This appeal is 2 CRA-5244-2019 of the year 2019 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

After perusal of the record and medical reports, it seems that victim's hymen was found old ruptured and there is no sign of forced rape and there is no other bodily injury, therefore, we are of Neelam @ Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142771527/

sentences.text: the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
3 CRA-5244-2019 List the matter for final hearing in due course.
